questionText:
The format of a single-precision floating-point number as per the IEEE 754 standard is:

Sign
(1bit)		Exponent
(8 bits)		Mantissa
(23 bits)

Choose the largest floating-point number among the following options.
options:
SignExponentMantissa
00111 11111111 1111 1111 1111 1111 111

SignExponentMantissa
01111 11101111 1111 1111 1111 1111 111

SignExponentMantissa
01111 11111111 1111 1111 1111 1111 111

SignExponentMantissa
00111 11110000 0000 0000 0000 0000 000
explanation:
In IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point format:
1. Sign bit ($S$): $0$ represents a positive number.
2. Exponent ($E$): 8-bit field with a bias of $127$.
• $E = 1111\ 1111_2 = 255$ is reserved for $\infty$ (if Mantissa $= 0$) or NaN (Not a Number, if Mantissa $\neq 0$). Option (C) has $E = 255$ and non-zero Mantissa, representing NaN.
• $E = 1111\ 1110_2 = 254$ is the maximum valid exponent value for normalized numbers ($254 - 127 = 127$).
3. Mantissa ($M$): 23-bit fractional part. All $1$s yields the maximum possible fractional value ($1 - 2^{-23}$).

Evaluating the options:
• Option (A): Exponent $127$, Mantissa all $1$s.
• Option (B): Maximum Exponent ($254$) and maximum Mantissa (all $1$s). This represents $M_{\text{max}} = (2 - 2^{-23}) \times 2^{127} \approx 3.4028 \times 10^{38}$, which is the largest finite single-precision number.
• Option (C): Represents NaN (Not a Number).
• Option (D): Exponent $127$, Mantissa $0$ (represents $1.0$).

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.
